# Bad debt events and socialized loss in Solana lending — facts

## How it works

- [statement] Kamino docs say socialize-loss should be a last resort. The position must be genuinely unrecoverable and all standard liquidation paths, including the bad-debt liquidation bonus, must be exhausted. The reserve should also have a credible loss-recovery plan, with insurance or treasury/curator backfill as examples. The docs describe no on-chain backfill mechanism. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://kamino.com/docs/curators/markets/emergency-controls · keywords: Bad debt events and socialized loss in Solana lending · also: https://kamino.com/docs/curators/markets/liquidations
- [statement] Until handle_bankruptcy runs, a marginfi loss is real but unbooked. The guide says the remaining depositors can never withdraw their full balance, and the last few to withdraw find too little left, in proportion to the bankrupt users' liabilities. The shortfall therefore lands on the slowest exiters, not pro rata. When a bankrupt user has several liabilities, the liquidator chooses which stay on the books, so the liquidator effectively chooses which banks absorb the bad debt. (high confidence) — https://github.com/0dotxyz/marginfi-v2/blob/main/guides/RISK_AND_LIQUIDATORS/BANKRUPTCY.md · keywords: Bad debt events and socialized loss in Solana lending · also: https://docs.0.xyz/protocol-overview/liquidation
- [statement] As of November 2025, marginfi's guide and the Project 0 docs both say handle_bankruptcy had never been executed in the main pool. The docs add that almost all bankruptcies occur in the Arena, where riskier assets see extreme volatility. They name three causes: liquidators not running properly (for example during congestion), an asset too illiquid to clear safely, and a price change faster than liquidators can respond. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2025-11-01) — https://github.com/0dotxyz/marginfi-v2/blob/main/guides/RISK_AND_LIQUIDATORS/BANKRUPTCY.md · keywords: Bad debt events and socialized loss in Solana lending · also: https://docs.0.xyz/protocol-overview/liquidation

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] To test whether a marginfi bank ever socialized a loss, index the program's LendingPoolBankHandleBankruptcyEvent (fields bad_debt, covered_amount, socialized_amount, premium_written_off) and watch for banks in operational state KilledByBankruptcy. A nonzero socialized_amount marks a lender haircut. I did not run this index. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mrgnlabs/marginfi-v2/blob/main/programs/marginfi/src/instructions/marginfi_group/handle_bankruptcy.rs · keywords: Bad debt events and socialized loss in Solana lending
- [statement] To detect a real socialization on-chain, look for the program's own signals. marginfi's handle_bankruptcy emits LendingPoolBankHandleBankruptcyEvent with bad_debt, covered_amount, socialized_amount and premium_written_off. klend logs 'Forgiving debt amount' when socialize-loss runs. Solend logs 'Instruction: Forgive Debt'. A rising share of socialized_amount over covered_amount shows the insurance vault ran short. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://github.com/0dotxyz/marginfi-v2/blob/main/programs/marginfi/src/instructions/marginfi_group/handle_bankruptcy.rs · keywords: Bad debt events and socialized loss in Solana lending · also: https://github.com/Kamino-Finance/klend/blob/master/programs/klend/src/lending_market/lending_operations.rs, https://github.com/solendprotocol/solana-program-library/blob/mainnet/token-lending/program/src/processor.rs

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Kamino lists auto-deleverage among the safeguards that 'can unwind risky positions before bad debt materializes'. The risk page gives no mechanics for it. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://kamino.com/docs/risk · keywords: Bad debt events and socialized loss in Solana lending
- [statement] marginfi runs an isolated pool for risky SPL assets that can be borrowed but not used as collateral. Squads' write-up presents this as the guard against bad debt from collateral that cannot be liquidated, and names no marginfi bad-debt incident. (low confidence) — https://squads.xyz/blog/marginfi-lending-protocol-solana · keywords: Bad debt events and socialized loss in Solana lending
- [statement] Jupiter Lend docs describe tick-based partial liquidation that restores a position only to the Liquidation Threshold. A position past the Liquidation Max Limit leaves the tick system and is fully liquidated to zero. The glossary defines 'Supply Absorb' as collateral absorbed by the protocol from an undercollateralized borrower and 'Borrow Absorb' as the borrower's debt settled during that absorption. The pages I read do not say who bears any residual shortfall (supplier haircut, reserve or treasury). (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/earn/lend/liquidation-mechanism · keywords: Bad debt events and socialized loss in Solana lending · also: https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/earn/lend/protocol-details
- [statement] Kamino Lend states it has no protocol-level insurance fund. Its risk page and its auto-deleverage page both say that bad debt, if it occurs, is socialized among lenders. Lending Vaults can add curator-funded first-loss capital ('insurance pools'), which the risk page calls a vault-level feature and not a protocol-wide backstop. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://kamino.com/docs/risk · keywords: Bad debt events and socialized loss in Solana lending · also: https://kamino.com/docs/risk/safeguards/auto-deleverage
- [statement] Kamino's auto-deleverage is a pre-emptive, borrower-side tool, not a loss-sharing step. The Risk Council triggers it by multisig vote after a risk signal, and borrowers get a default 72-hour margin call that the council may shorten or waive. The docs say lenders are never affected. They cite the Aave CRV and Solend whale incidents as the motivation, and give an example of $50M of loans against $5M of market sell capacity that would otherwise end as bad debt socialized among lenders. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://kamino.com/docs/risk/safeguards/auto-deleverage · keywords: Bad debt events and socialized loss in Solana lending · also: https://kamino.com/docs/risk
- [statement] Jupiter Lend's vaults program (Instadapp/Fluid lineage) exposes no write-off or socialize instruction; its instructions are init_*, update_*, init_position, operate, liquidate, rebalance and get_exchange_prices. Positions beyond the liquidation max limit tick are 'absorbed': their debt and collateral move into vault-level absorbed totals (code comment: 'handle bad debt above max limit'), and a liquidator clears that pool by passing absorb = true. The sources read do not say who bears any shortfall left in the absorbed pool, and the separate Liquidity Layer program was not checked, so the loss-allocation rule is unverified. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://github.com/Instadapp/fluid-solana-programs/blob/main/programs/vaults/src/module/user.rs · keywords: Bad debt events and socialized loss in Solana lending · also: https://github.com/Instadapp/fluid-solana-programs/blob/main/programs/vaults/src/lib.rs, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Instadapp/fluid-solana-programs/main/README.md
- [statement] The Solana Compass podcast notes (AI-generated, unverified) say marginfi's co-founder models risk assuming only in-house liquidators operate in extreme markets, and that Solend's founder saw many third-party liquidators go offline during the FTX crisis despite high profits. This matches the 'liquidators not running' cause that marginfi's docs list for bankruptcy. (low confidence) — https://solanacompass.com/learn/Lightspeed/the-marginfi-vs-solend-debate-lessons-from-msols-depeg · keywords: Bad debt events and socialized loss in Solana lending · also: https://docs.0.xyz/protocol-overview/liquidation

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Kamino's risk page states 'Kamino Lend does not operate a protocol-level insurance fund'. It says bad debt, when it occurs, is socialized among lenders. Lending Vaults can instead offer curator-funded first-loss capital (insurance pools), described as a vault-level feature rather than a protocol-wide mechanism. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://kamino.com/docs/risk · keywords: Bad debt events and socialized loss in Solana lending
- [statement] Kamino Lend has no protocol-level insurance fund, per its risk page. The page says the $0 bad-debt record reflects the risk framework 'rather than a backstop fund'. Only Lending Vaults carry curator-funded first-loss capital (insurance pools), a vault-level feature and not a protocol-wide one. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://kamino.com/docs/risk · keywords: Bad debt events and socialized loss in Solana lending

## Facts and statements

- [statement] marginfi-v2's handle_bankruptcy instruction first verifies the account is bankrupt, then computes bad_debt from liability shares. It sets covered_by_insurance = min(bad_debt, available_insurance_fund), moves that amount from the insurance vault to the liquidity vault, and passes the remainder to bank.socialize_loss(). If socialize_loss signals kill_bank, the bank's operational_state becomes KilledByBankruptcy. The caller must be group admin or risk_admin unless the bank sets PERMISSIONLESS_BAD_DEBT_SETTLEMENT_FLAG. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://github.com/mrgnlabs/marginfi-v2/blob/main/programs/marginfi/src/instructions/marginfi_group/handle_bankruptcy.rs · keywords: Bad debt events and socialized loss in Solana lending
- [statement] Solend, Nov 2 2022: an attacker spent about 100k USDC to inflate USDH on Saber. Solend relied only on the Switchboard oracle fed from that Saber pool. The attacker spammed the Saber account to block same-slot arbitrage, then borrowed against the inflated price from the Stable, Coin98 and Kamino isolated pools. The resulting bad debt was $1.26M. Per Ackee, Solend DAO proposals SLND5 and SLND6 made users whole. (low confidence) — https://ackee.xyz/blog/?p=455 · keywords: Bad debt events and socialized loss in Solana lending
- [statement] Solend, Nov 2 2022: an attacker pumped USDH on Saber and borrowed against the inflated price, leaving $1.26M of bad debt in the Stable, Coin98 and Kamino isolated pools. Solend priced USDH from a Switchboard feed that read only that Saber pool. Per Ackee, a first attempt on Oct 28 (200k USDC) was arbitraged away in the same slot. On Nov 2 the attacker spent 100k USDC and spammed or write-locked the Saber account so no same-slot arbitrage could occur. Solend disabled the three pools. (high confidence) — https://ackee.xyz/blog/?p=455 · keywords: Bad debt events and socialized loss in Solana lending · also: https://www.theblock.co/news/defi/2022-11-02-solend-exploited-attack-182055, https://www.coindesk.com/business/2022/11/02/defi-protocol-solend-struck-by-126m-oracle-exploit
